comparisons.peer_summary: Average loans increased 2% year-over-year, driven by growth in Services (5%), Markets (6%), and USPB (7%). Decreases occurred in Banking (-6%) and Wealth (-1%), primarily due to regulatory capital optimization efforts.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C reported year-over-year growth in their loan portfolios for 2024, driven by commercial and consumer lending segments. BAC disclosed a $42.1 billion increase in loans and leases, primarily driven by commercial loans. Similarly, C reported a 2% year-over-year increase in average loans, with growth in Services (driven by export and agency finance, working capital loans) and USPB (Retail Banking mortgages and Branded Cards), while noting decreases in Banking and Wealth due to regulatory capital optimization.

sentences.text: Loans and leases increased $42.1 billion primarily driven by growth in commercial loans.
On an average basis, loans increased 2% year-over-year and were relatively unchanged sequentially.
• Services increased 5% year-over-year, primarily driven by strong demand in TTS for export and agency finance, as well as working capital loans.

• USPB increased 7% year-over-year, driven by growth in Retail Banking due to an increase in mortgage loans as a result of lower refinancings due to a higher interest rate environment and higher mortgage originations, as well as Branded Cards due to lower card payment rates and higher card spend volume.

comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024 from $1.14 billion in 2023, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: While BAC focuses on the gross growth of its loan and lease portfolio, GS discloses the expense associated with credit risks within those loans, specifically the provision for credit losses. Both disclosures concern the financial performance of the lending books in 2024. BAC reported a $42.1 billion increase in loans and leases. In contrast, GS reported a $1.54 billion provision for credit losses, driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio. GS's 2023 provision was lower at $1.14 billion, similar to how BAC's loan growth accelerated compared to its 2023 increase of $8.0 billion.
